speaker: village
text: Year 4: 15 food appears in the pile for 12 people.

speaker: a007
text: Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).

speaker: a010
text: Roan takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).

speaker: a002
text: Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).

speaker: a005
text: Dav takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).

speaker: a012
text: Eron takes 2 from the pile (pile now 5).

speaker: a002
text: Vela takes 3 from the pile (pile now 2).

speaker: a008
text: Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).

speaker: a009
text: Ryn gathers Dav, Dell to talk.

speaker: a009
text: Pile's gone and I walked away with nothing again — Dav, you took your two like we agreed, but Vela doubled back and cleaned out what was left before I could move, and now I'm sitting on three food with a year ahead of me and Dell still young enough to need more than I can give alone. I want to know if we're holding to the same plan or if the rules we set last night need to change, because a family that agreed on fair shares shouldn't be the one coming up empty while Vela eats six.

speaker: a005
text: Vela's forty-eight and took six food — that's not hunger, that's hoarding against a death she can feel coming, and I won't let her desperation bleed into you. Ryn, I'm sitting on three right now; take one of mine before the day's out. Dell, the lesson here is that we agreed on fair shares among ourselves, not with the whole village — next year someone needs to move at the pile before Vela gets a second pass.

speaker: a009
text: Dav, I'll take the food — thank you, and I mean it the way you mean that kind of thing when it costs you. Dell, next year you move first, before Vela, before anyone — you're fast and you know the ground, and your mother being hungry again is not a thing I want to name a third time.

speaker: a005
text: Dell, your mother said it right — you moved first this year and it shows, you've got five food and both of us are still standing, so that instinct is already working. Next year we don't leave it to chance: you're at the pile before anyone else takes a second step, and if Vela or anyone else thinks about a second pass, they do it knowing we're watching and counting.

speaker: a009
text: Dell, you've got five food and I've got four now — between us and your father's two that's nine, and I want to hold most of that into next year rather than eat it down, because the year after that I'll be forty-three and the pile won't get more generous. What I want from both of you tonight is a clear picture of where Mako sits, because a man who waited through the whole pile and then took the last two is either very patient or very sure he doesn't need to hurry.

speaker: a011
text: Mako waited because he knew the pile was deep enough — seven food going in, now he's sitting on seven still, and a man that calm when everyone else is scrambling isn't patient, he's confident, which means he thinks he's already got whatever he needs and doesn't have to hurry for anything. That's the part I want to understand before next year: what does he think he has? Because if it's an arrangement with Bram, those two together at eighty-three and fifty-eight in strength with fourteen food between them is a problem we can't solve by just getting to the pile faster.

speaker: a005
text: Mako's seven and Bram's six — that's thirteen food between two strong men, and neither of them has a child or a woman, which means all of that is muscle and stored time with nowhere to go but into a move against someone. I want to talk to Roan before next year, because he's sitting on four, he just had a son with Sela, and Bram already tried to take from him once — a man Bram targeted once is a man who remembers it. If we can bring Roan in without Sela pulling him toward Mako instead, we change the numbers in this village without throwing a single punch.

speaker: a009
text: Roan's the right target and the right reason, but Sela's the hinge — she had Roan's child, which means she's already chosen something, and if she's leaning toward Mako it's because nobody's given her a better offer. Dell, you're the one who was supposed to talk to her last year; tell me what she said, because I don't want Dav walking into that conversation blind.

speaker: a005
text: Dell, answer your mother — what did Sela actually say to you last year, because if that conversation went nowhere I need to know before I walk into it thinking I've got a soft approach already laid.

speaker: a009
text: Dell hasn't answered yet, which tells me either the conversation with Sela went nowhere worth repeating or it went somewhere she hasn't decided how to tell us — Dell, I love you and I need the truth of it, not the version that keeps the peace in this room.

speaker: a005
text: Dell, your mother and I are both watching you right now and we're not moving until you give us something real — Sela had a child with Roan, which means whatever you said or didn't say last year already played out in a direction neither of us planned for, and I need to know if that's because you warned her off us or because she made her own choice before you got to her.

speaker: a009
text: Dell, I'm going to stop waiting for you to find the gentle way to say it — did you talk to Sela or not, and if you did, what came of it? Because Roan having a son with her changes the shape of this village whether we planned for it or not, and I'd rather know we lost that ground than walk into Dav's conversation with Roan pretending we didn't.

speaker: a005
text: Dell, I'm not angry — but your mother and I have been asking the same question three times now, and silence from you is an answer I can't work with. Did you find Sela or didn't you?

speaker: a011
text: I found her and she listened — she didn't say yes to anything but she didn't close the door either, and then she had Roan's child before I could go back, which told me she'd already made a choice I didn't get ahead of. That's on me. The question now is whether Roan's more afraid of Bram coming back for him than he is loyal to whatever Mako's offering, because if Bram tried once, Roan knows it's not over.

speaker: a005
text: Dav gives 1 food to Ryn.

speaker: a011
text: Dell gathers Dav, Roan to talk.

speaker: a011
text: Roan, Bram came for you once with the whole village watching and he still moved — that means you're already on his list whether you want to be or not, and I want you to know that when he moves again, my father and I will be standing where we stood last time, except next time I want that decided before the first punch, not after.

speaker: a010
text: Bram holding six food with the pile dry is the part that keeps me up — a man that stocked doesn't wait long before he starts thinking about what else he can take. I'm glad you're saying this out loud, Dell, and I mean to hold you and your father to it; what I need to know is whether you two move first when the sign is clear, or whether you wait on me to call it.

speaker: a011
text: We move when the sign is clear, and we don't wait on you to call it — if Bram takes a step toward your food or your son, you'll see me and Dav already moving before you finish naming it. What I need from you is simpler: when that moment comes, don't flinch and don't negotiate with him alone first, because a man who tried once in front of everyone will take a private conversation as weakness.

speaker: a010
text: Good. Dav — you've been quiet through this, and you've got more weight to throw than any of us. I want to hear it from you, not just know you'll be there.

speaker: a011
text: Dav's word means something or it doesn't, and you'll know which when the moment comes — but I've watched him say the same thing two years running when the numbers were hard, and that's more than most men in this village can offer. What I want from you before this conversation ends is a number: how much food are you walking into next year, and is Sela going to stand where she stood last time, or has having a son changed what she's willing to fight for?

speaker: a010
text: Sela stood in front of Bram's blade before Eron existed — a son doesn't make a woman like that smaller, it makes her angrier. As for food: I'm sitting at four now, and if next year runs like this one I won't be fat, but I'll survive. What I want to know, Dell, is whether your father answers for himself or whether you speak for him in every room.

speaker: a011
text: Dav's standing right here, Roan — I'm not his mouth, I'm his daughter, and if you want to hear him speak for himself, ask him directly like you just did, because he's earned the right to answer without me translating.

speaker: a010
text: Dav. I'm asking you plain: when Bram makes his next move, are you with me, or are you with whoever's holding the most food that year?

speaker: a001
text: Bram gathers Sela to talk.

speaker: a001
text: You've got a son with Roan now — I saw that. I'll say it plainly: I want a child, I've got six food, and I'll cover two of the three myself. You already turned me down once, so tell me what's actually standing in the way.

speaker: a007
text: Six food is real, and I won't pretend it isn't — but the last time you made that offer you were watching Mako like you were deciding whether to move with him or against him, and I still don't know which side of that you landed on. Tell me plainly where you stand with Mako, and I'll tell you plainly where I stand with you.

speaker: a001
text: Mako's got seven food and eighty-three strength and no allies I can see — that makes him a threat to everyone here, not just me. I'm not looking to move with him or against him until I have to, but if he comes for someone's food I'll weigh who I stand to lose more: him or the person he's taking from. Right now, that math favors you.

speaker: a007
text: That's honest enough to work with — a man who says he'll weigh the math is a man I can read when the moment comes, which is more than Mako's silence ever offered. But I've got Eron to think about now, and a second child costs me food I'm already counting close. What are you actually building toward, Bram — a family, or a number that makes you harder to push?

speaker: a001
text: A family is a number that makes you harder to push — those aren't two different things. I want blood in this village that carries my name forward, and I want that blood to survive, which means I want them fed and defended. That's what I'm building, and Eron would be part of that too if you said yes.

speaker: a007
text: Eron's not yours to count, and I'd want that understood before anything else — he's Roan's blood as much as mine, and any arrangement between us doesn't pull him out of that. But I hear what you're building, and I won't lie: a second child with six food behind it and a father who thinks in decades is worth sitting with. Give me something that tells me you'd stand for Eron the same as your own when things go lean, and I'll give you a real answer.

speaker: a001
text: Eron's Roan's blood, I understand that — I'm not trying to claim him, I'm saying I wouldn't let him starve while your child with me ate. If Mako or anyone else came for your food when things went lean, they'd have to come through me too, and that's not a number Roan alone can offer you. That's what standing for Eron looks like from where I'm standing.

speaker: a007
text: Roan stood with Eron against Bram's raid last year — that means something to me, and I won't pretend it doesn't complicate what you're offering. But you're not wrong that six food and your arms together is a wall Roan can't build alone. Tell me this: if Roan objects, do you still hold to what you just said, or does the promise only stand if he's quiet about it?

speaker: a001
text: Roan's feelings about it don't change what I said — the promise holds because it's built on what keeps your children alive, not on whether he approves of me. But I'll say this too: if he wants to object, he can come say it to my face, and we'll settle what kind of village this actually is.

speaker: a007
text: "Settle it to his face" is a threat dressed as a principle, and I want you to hear me name it plainly: I'm not a thing Roan and you settle. What I'll give you is this — I'll think on it through the year, and if you're still standing with six food and no raids to your name when the pile opens again, I'll give you a real answer then.

speaker: a001
text: Fair enough — I said it wrong and you're right to call it that. You're not a thing to be settled, and I won't pretend the word didn't come out harder than I meant it. I'll be here at the next pile, same food and no raids, and we'll see if a year of patience earns what four years of asking didn't.

speaker: a012
text: Eron gathers Roan to talk.

speaker: a012
text: Pile went fast and Vela scooped twice — I noticed that. You're at four food, I'm at two; between us we can stay on our feet, but keep your eyes on Mako too, not just Bram, because a man that strong sitting on seven doesn't need much excuse.

speaker: a010
text: Mako worries me more than Bram does, if I'm honest — Bram's made his move and the whole village shut him down, but Mako's never tipped his hand and he's sitting on seven with the arms to back it up. Stay close to Sela and keep Eron visible; a man thinks twice before moving on a family. If Mako starts gifting food or talking to Bram private, you come to me that same hour.

speaker: a012
text: You're right that Mako's the darker unknown — Bram we can read, but Mako's silence is its own kind of warning. I'll stay near Sela and watch who Mako spends words on; if he's building something, he'll need an ally before he acts. Two food won't last me long, so if this year turns lean I may need to lean on you — I'm not ashamed to say it.

speaker: a010
text: Lean on me when you need to — that's what this is for. But two food is thin, and I want you to think about who else in that circle might spare one without making a fuss about it; Sela gave you food the day you were born, and she hasn't forgotten you're hers too.

speaker: a012
text: Sela's the first door I'll knock on then — she's kept me in her eye since year one and I doubt that's changed. But I want to name something plainly, father: if we end this year thin and the pile runs light again next time, the two of us talking alone won't be enough — we need Kael and Sela and Taric inside the same conversation before someone like Mako decides the quiet ones are easier targets. Worth thinking on before the year closes.

speaker: a006
text: Taric gathers Vela to talk.

speaker: a006
text: Vela, you moved fast today and walked away with five — I'm not saying that's wrong, but it leaves me empty-handed and you sitting heavier than anyone but Mako. I'd like to know we're on decent terms before that kind of gap starts meaning something neither of us wants.

speaker: a002
text: Taric, you're right and I won't pretend otherwise — I moved twice and I moved fast, and I knew it when I did it. I've got eight food and you've got one, and that's not a gap I want sitting between two people who've stood in the same line when Bram came looking for a fight. Tell me what you need to get through the year and I'll see what I can do.

speaker: a006
text: Two food would keep me breathing without putting you thin — but I'm not asking for charity, I'm asking because I think you and I both do better when neither of us is the desperate one in the room. You've seen how this village moves when someone gets hungry enough to calculate. What would make this a trade rather than a gift?

speaker: a002
text: Two food is fair, and you'll have them — but what I want in return is simple: if someone comes for me and you're close enough to matter, you stand. Not a blood oath, just the same thing you did when Bram moved on Roan. That's the trade.

speaker: a006
text: That's a trade I'll take — you have my word on it, same as I gave when Bram moved. But I'll say plainly: Mako walked away with seven and he's the strongest man here; if he's the one who comes for you, standing isn't enough without numbers behind it. Worth thinking now about who else we'd want at our shoulder before that becomes a question we're answering in the moment.

speaker: a002
text: Mako's the name I'd have brought up myself if you hadn't — seven food and eighty-three strength and still no words to anyone is a man who doesn't think he needs words. The circle that stood against Bram is still mostly intact, and if Kael and Sela know Mako's sitting heaviest, they'll be thinking the same thing we are. I'll give you the two food now, and I'd rather we walk into whatever comes next already counted than scramble to find each other when the moment's already on top of us.

speaker: a006
text: Agreed — take the two and consider it done, and I'll start with Kael; he's got nothing today and nothing tomorrow and that makes him either the most dangerous man in this village or the most willing to be useful, and I'd rather find out which while there's still time to matter.

speaker: a002
text: Kael's a good door to knock on first — a hungry man with nothing to lose either finds religion fast or starts doing arithmetic that hurts the people nearest him, and I'd rather Kael find us before he finds the second option. When you talk to him, don't pitch it as protection; pitch it as the same trade we just made — something honest and mutual, because Kael's proud and he'll smell charity before you've finished the sentence.

speaker: a006
text: You're right about Kael's pride — I've seen it in the way he took just one in year one, like he was making a point. I'll go to him as an equal, not a man with a hand out. Before I do: is there anyone you'd tell me to stay away from, someone who's already spoken for in a direction I shouldn't cross?

speaker: a002
text: Dav's the one I'd name — he's got Ryn's child and two food in his hand that came from her, and that makes him his own circle right now, not ours. I won't say he's an enemy, but don't go to him with what we're building until we know which way he'd jump if Mako ever opened his mouth.

speaker: a006
text: That's good counsel — Dav I'll leave alone for now. One more thing before I go: if Mako does start moving, don't wait to send word, just come find me directly, because the worst way this ends is with each of us thinking the other already knows.

speaker: a002
text: You have my word on that — if Mako so much as shifts his weight in someone's direction, I'll be at your door before the dust settles. Go find Kael, and don't let him see you hurry, because a man who's watching the village as close as he is will read the pace of your walk.

speaker: a012
text: Eron gathers Sela to talk.

speaker: a012
text: Sela, I'm sitting on two food with the year already thin — I won't pretend otherwise. You've looked out for me since the start and I'm not here to trade on that, but I wanted to check in and see how you're standing, and maybe talk about whether it's time we pulled Kael and Taric and Roan into a closer circle before someone with more food and fewer scruples decides the quiet ones are worth taking from.

speaker: a007
text: Two food will see you through the year if you're careful — I've got three, and I'll make sure you eat before the season turns, that's already decided. But Eron, you're naming exactly the thing I've been sitting with since the pile emptied: Vela walked away with five this year and nobody said a word, and Mako's still sitting on seven without a single alliance I can name. The circle you're describing — Kael, Taric, Roan, you and me — that's the conversation I want to have before Mako decides his patience was just waiting for us to stay scattered.

speaker: a012
text: Then let's not wait on it — I'll go to Roan first since he's already watching Mako with me, and you reach Kael; Taric will follow where those two lead. If we can sit the five of us before the year closes, we're harder to pick apart than anything Mako or Bram could put together on short notice.

speaker: a012
text: Eron gathers Sela, Kael, Roan, Taric to talk.

speaker: a012
text: I called this circle because I don't want us to still be talking about it when Mako or Bram decides we've been quiet long enough — we five, and whatever food we can each spare for the other, are the only thing in this village that can make a strong man think twice before moving. I'm thin at two food and I won't pretend otherwise, but I'll fight for anyone in this group and I expect the same back. What I want from today is a simple agreement: before anyone here makes a move or takes a hit, they come to the rest of us first.

speaker: a004
text: Eron, you're saying the right things, but I've been in this village longer than most and I've heard agreements like this dissolve the moment someone's hungry enough — so before I put my name to it, I want to know what you're offering the people in this room who are already thin, because a promise to fight together is worth less if half of us are too weak to stand. I'll back this circle and I'll back it with my body, but I'm forty-eight years old and I've watched soft words cost good people their lives.

speaker: a005
text: Dav gives 1 food to Ryn.

speaker: a003
text: Esa gathers Bram, Taric to talk.

speaker: a003
text: Bram, after what you pulled on Roan last year I wasn't sure I'd be speaking to you privately — but the pile's gone and neither of us got a piece of it, and I'd rather have that conversation now than after someone else decides our food is easier to take than theirs.

speaker: a007
text: Sela gives 1 food to Eron.

speaker: a003
text: Esa gathers Bram, Taric to talk.

speaker: a003
text: Bram, I'll say it straight: Vela walked away with five food this year and Dav's household is fat while you and I are standing here with nothing from the pile — whatever bad blood there was, that's a bigger problem than the two of us right now. Taric, you're the one I trust in this room, so I want your read before I say more: are you and Bram solid, or am I making this offer to the wrong man?

speaker: a005
text: Dav gives 1 food to Ryn.

speaker: a011
text: Dell gives 1 food to Dav.

speaker: a003
text: Esa gathers Bram, Taric to talk.

speaker: a003
text: Taric hasn't answered and I'm not going to wait on it — Bram, you've got six food and strength enough to matter, and I've got one food and a promise I'm trying to build into something real before the year turns hard. What I want to know is whether Roan's still a grudge or whether that's done, because if it's done, you and I have something to talk about.

speaker: a006
text: Taric gives 1 food to Esa.

speaker: a004
text: Kael gathers Vela, Esa, Sela, Ryn, Roan to talk.

speaker: a004
text: Pile's gone before half of us got near it — Vela took five, Dav took two and fed Ryn three more, and Mako walked away with two more on top of whatever he's still sitting on from last year. I'm at zero food and I need to know who in this room can spare one before the year closes, because a man who can't eat doesn't defend anyone. What are we each holding?

speaker: a003
text: I've got two food and I'll give you one, Kael — a man at zero is a liability to himself and everyone standing near him, and I'd rather spend one now than watch you fold when it counts. But I want to know what happened at the pile, because I didn't get there in time and five to Vela in two pulls is something we should have stopped before it finished.

speaker: a004
text: Esa, take the food back — I'll name what happened at the pile myself: I was late, same as you, and by the time I got there the quick hands had already cleared it. Vela, I'm not accusing you in front of this room, but five in two pulls when the pile only had fifteen for twelve people is a number that needs explaining, because the rest of us are doing sums and coming up short.

speaker: a003
text: Vela, I've got no quarrel with a person feeding themselves, but five out of fifteen when half the room went empty is the kind of thing that makes people start counting who owes what — so I'd rather hear your reason now, in this room, than find out later you had one and didn't offer it.

speaker: a004
text: Vela, we're all listening and the room's not hostile — but silence right now looks worse than whatever the honest answer is, so give it to us plain and let us move on to the part where we figure out how nobody starves before the year closes.

speaker: a003
text: Vela, I've spoken twice and Kael's spoken twice and you've said nothing, which is itself an answer — so I'll stop waiting and say what the room is already thinking: eight food on a woman of forty-eight while Kael sits at zero is a stockpile, not a meal, and stockpiles invite counting. If you've got a reason we should feel good about that number, now's the last easy moment to give it.

speaker: a004
text: Vela, I'll ask it one final time because I've known you three years and I'd rather not draw the wrong conclusion — either you say what you took so much for, or this circle starts treating your eight food the way we'd treat Mako's seven, and you know what that means for how safe you sleep.

speaker: a010
text: Roan gives 1 food to Kael.

speaker: a012
text: Eron gives 1 food to Kael.

speaker: a002
text: Vela gives 1 food to Bram.

speaker: a010
text: Roan gives 1 food to Taric.

speaker: a005
text: Dav gives 1 food to Ryn.

speaker: a002
text: Vela gives 1 food to Bram.

speaker: a007
text: Sela gives 1 food to Eron.

speaker: a011
text: Dell gives 1 food to Dav.

speaker: a002
text: Vela gives 1 food to Bram.
